q: One way to balance oxidation-reduction equations is by keeping track of the electron transfer using the ____ of each of the atoms.
e: One way to balance oxidation-reduction equations is by keeping track of the electron transfer using the oxidation numbers of each of the atoms. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.

q: Balance the oxidation number changes by multiplying appropriate coefficients to make the total increase in oxidation number ____ to the total decrease in oxidation number.
e: Balance the oxidation number changes by multiplying appropriate coefficients to make the total increase in oxidation number equal to the total decrease in oxidation number. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.

e: In the half-equation method, the equation is separated into two half-reactions, one for oxidation and one for reduction. The equation is separated into two half-reactions, one for oxidation and one for reduction.

q: Acidic condition usually implies a solution with an excess of ____ concentration, hence making the solution acidic.
e: Acidic condition usually implies a solution with an excess of H^+ concentration, hence making the solution acidic. Extra hydrogen ions are what make the solution acidic.

q: Bases produce ____ ions in solution; hence, balancing a redox reaction in basic condition requires them.
e: Bases produce OH^- ions in solution. hence, balancing a redox reaction in basic condition requires them.
